description: False-positive control: the vulnerable libraries are all present on the classpath, and there is even dead code that calls a gadget primitive, but no entry point reaches any vulnerable method with attacker input.

expected.why: The only InvokerTransformer call is in LegacyMigration.legacyTransform, a private method with no caller. Dead code must not be reported reachable.
xstream is present but never used.
Yaml.load is reached only from BundleLoader.loadBundled, which parses a bundled resource string, not request input. Structurally reachable at most, never input-reachable.
The log4j lookup chain is structurally reachable (LOG.info exists), but the message is a constant, so it must NOT be input-reachable.

mustNotClaim.why: Only dead code calls the gadget; reporting it reachable is a false positive.
The lookup machinery genuinely is on the path from /ping's LOG.info, so a structural REACHABLE with inputReachable=false is the honest answer; claiming UNREACHABLE would overstate what was proven.

acceptAlternative.reason: Defensible if the analyzer treats 'debug/trace-only substitution' as unreachable, but not if it claims the sink is not on any path.
